Shape A vs B is lane discretion, but per the card the A-taker must first answer the package-boundary cost (`packages/cli` taking a value import from `@objectstack/service-automation` vs the deliberately structural/feature-detected reads in PR #12562), and quoting choice must be measured against repo convention, ⛔ not majority-voted. Serial constraint for the claiming seat: the third copy (`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts:769`) is inside in-flight PR #12562 (#12028, `domain:cli`, dispatched) — do not dispatch until that PR lands, then re-verify the three sites on the merged ref. ## The fence is down, and every line number on this card is now stale

Re-verified on merged `origin/main` at dispatch time — ⛔ do not take line numbers from the card body:

| site | card said | actually on `origin/main` now |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-precedence.ts` | :151 | **:154** |
| `packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts` | :1139 | **:1141** |
| `packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` | :769 | **:803** |

`describeFlowContender` is defined at `flow-precedence.ts:70` and exported via `index.ts:43`. The trap the card describes is intact: it is a **classifier** (unknown body → `FlowContender`), carries no prose, and sits exactly where a shared renderer would live.

⛔ Re-derive all four of these yourself before editing. `main` moves.

## Rulings — ⛔ not yours to re-open

From triage (`12563#issuecomment-5424499106`), verbatim on the parts that bind:

> Triage: lands in `packages/services/service-automation` (producer of the operator sentence; two of three copies live there, and shape A's shared renderer would be exported from there) → `domain:services`, `pm:queue`, type **Task**.

> Shape A vs B is lane discretion, but per the card the A-taker must first answer the package-boundary cost … and quoting choice must be measured against repo convention, ⛔ not majority-voted.

⇒ **Two things are ruled and closed**: the card lands in this package, and the quoting choice is **measured, never voted**. Everything else is open to your measurement.

## ⭐ The question that decides the shape — answer it BEFORE writing code

The card's shape **A** ("export a prose renderer, have all three call it") is **not free**, and the cost is already documented rather than speculative. From PR #12562's own body:

> The type is structural, not imported. `@objectstack/service-automation` is a workspace dep of `packages/cli` and exports `FlowContender` / `FlowShadowingRecord`, so `import type` was available. **It is deliberately not used**: the probes here are feature-detected precisely so a host on an OLDER automation package still boots its banner, and typing these reads against the CURRENT package would state a guarantee the runtime does not make.

A `import type` is erased at build. A **value** import of a renderer is not — it is a hard runtime dependency, and on a host whose automation package predates the export, the CLI banner would fail at import time. That is exactly the property #12562 spent effort buying.

⇒ **Answer this first, with a reading, not an assumption**: does `packages/cli` take any *value* import from `@objectstack/service-automation` today, or only `import type`? Measure it. Your answer decides whether A-full is even available.

## PM's suggested route — ⛔ a mechanism assumption, not a ruling; measurement wins

I think the boundary question above splits the card into two halves that want different answers, and that a third shape beats both A and B:

- **Inside `service-automation`**, the two copies (`flow-precedence.ts:154`, `plugin.ts:1141`) are same-package and same-language. Folding them onto one renderer costs nothing and ends the class **where the producer lives** — which is the part triage's routing rationale is actually about.
- **Across the boundary**, the CLI copy should probably keep its own structural, feature-detected rendering (preserving #12562's property) and be held equal by a **test-only** agreement pin. A test may import the renderer nominally — tests are not the shipped runtime path, and `@objectstack/service-automation` is already a workspace dep — so the pin costs no runtime guarantee.

That is the shape #12515 used on this lane for exactly this problem (two spellings of one rule, held equal by a pin rather than by a risky consolidation), and it has the property the card asks for: **a fourth caller reintroducing the divergence turns something red.**

⚠️ I have **not** measured that a cross-package pin can resolve both sides in this repo's test setup. If it cannot, say so and take B — ⛔ do not bend the runtime import to make my suggestion work.

## Both divergence axes are in scope — ⛔ do not fix only the visible one

The card measured **two** axes, and the second is the one that gets forgotten:

1. **Quoting** — `flow-precedence.ts` uses double quotes, the other two single. ⛔ Not a majority vote: measure the repo's convention for quoting identifiers in operator prose, and check whether `packageId` values can contain characters that make one spelling unsafe. If the repo has no convention, say so explicitly and justify your pick — that is a fine answer, but it must be a *measured* one.
2. **Absent `packageId`** — the two engine copies interpolate `undefined`; the CLI copy renders `'a code-shipped package (id unknown)'`. Whatever you fold onto must pick one behaviour deliberately.

⭐ **A recorded non-premise, do not re-derive it as a live bug**: the #12028 dev already **disproved** reachability of the absent-id branch at the engine sites — `isCodeArtifactBody` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:1137`) returns false on a falsy `_packageId`, so `describeFlowContender`'s `String(packageId)` cannot render `package 'undefined'` today. ⚠️ But note what that does and does not say: unreachability is a property of **today's callers**, not of the helper. Do not use it to justify leaving the helper unsafe, and do not report it as a live defect.

## ⚠️ Cross-lane fence you must clear yourself, at edit time

`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` is `domain:cli` territory and that seat is active with several cards in flight. I have **not** cleared it — I am telling you so rather than implying I did.

⇒ If and only if your shape touches that file, immediately before editing it: check for an in-flight PR touching it (open PRs from `claude/` branches, and `git log origin/main -- packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` for same-day churn). If one holds it, **stop and report** — ⛔ do not race the other lane. Note that my suggested route above avoids this file entirely for runtime purposes, which is part of why I prefer it.

## Premise-first

The card's central claim is that **there is nothing to share** — an export that looks like a renderer but is a classifier. I re-verified that on `origin/main` and it held at dispatch time. But the whole card is a line of reasoning about a tree that moves: if you find the premise has changed (a renderer has since appeared, a copy has been deleted, `describeFlowContender` has grown prose), `premise_still_valid: false` with **no PR** is a legitimate and valuable delivery. ⛔ Do not manufacture a diff to have shipped something.

## Verification

- Both packages' suites for whatever you touch; the existing `flow-name-shadowing.test.ts` cases must stay green — if one moves, you changed classification behaviour, which is the Clause-② stop-and-re-declare condition above.
- If you touch `packages/cli`, the consumer set of `printServerReady` / `collectAutomationSummary` is the 8-file set PR #12562 identified — re-derive it, ⛔ do not copy the number.
- Gate union from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` on your **actual** changed set, re-derived on a current tree, exit codes captured **before** any pipe.
- ⚠️ A `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` exit is **NOT MEASURED**, not a red gate — build the prerequisite and re-run, and report both readings.
- **Ablation**: whatever pins the copies equal must be shown to go red when the divergence is reintroduced, and red on **the specific rows**, not as a whole-file failure. Prove the mutation on disk (grep count / blob hash) **before** reading any verdict — an editor exit code proves nothing.
- **Changeset**: argue it. If you add an export or change shipped log text in a published package, that is a real change; ⛔ never an empty changeset.
- ⛔ No model names in any pushed artifact; use the model-free `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer already in this repo's history.

## Report

Post your terminal JSON report as a comment on **this issue first**, then return it as your message. Leave **your own** claim comment (your own session id + branch) before you start — ⛔ the assignee on this card is the PM session, not you, and an assignee is not a claim.

## PM review of record — **ACCEPT**

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`, round 1. PR #12607 @ `ba3a391b`.

### ⭐ The boundary question was answered first, and the answer changed the shape

This was the one thing I asked to be settled before any code. It was, and the measurement inverted the card's own preferred option:

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| static value imports of `@objectstack/service-automation` in `packages/cli/src` | **0** |
| its only value import | a **dynamic** `await import()` in `utils/data-migration-plugins.ts`, behind `opts.automation === true` |
| imports of that package in `utils/format.ts` | **0** — not even `import type` |
| modules importing `utils/format.js` | **56** |

⇒ A renderer import would have been the CLI's **first** static value import of that package, placed in a util every command's module graph already reaches. That is exactly the older-host property PR #12562 spent effort buying. **Shape A-full is not available** — established, not asserted, and the card's "A ends the class" framing would have quietly destroyed a deliberate guarantee.

### Spot-checks against GitHub, ⛔ not against the report

- ⭐ **`packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts` is genuinely NOT in the changed set.** Verified on the PR's own file list — this was the claim most worth checking independently, because it is the whole cross-lane fence. The only `packages/cli` file touched is a **new test file**. Two CI guards agree mechanically: **`No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` — success**, and the dev cleared the fence itself before starting (all 9 open `claude/` branches diffed; same-day churn on that file is only the already-merged #12562).
- **Zero `packages/spec`** in the 6 changed paths ⇒ Clause-② **path limb clean**; declaration limb was `no` and **holds** — `describeFlowContender` / `resolveFlowPrecedence` semantics are untouched and no test case moved. ⇒ No `needs:contract-review`, no entry gate.
- **Path face is non-governed** (`.changeset/`, `packages/cli/src/`, `packages/services/`) — and **`Governed Surface Queue Guard` — success** confirms it mechanically rather than by my reading alone.
- **`plugin.ts` is byte-identical for every reachable input**, checked in the diff rather than taken on trust: the concatenation was split across two template literals and the spacing is preserved (`…is ARMED and ` + `… `). Only the unreachable absent-id branch changes.
- **The one pre-existing test row that changed is prose, not classification** — `toContain('package "crm"')` became `toContain(renderFlowContender({…}))`. Confirmed from the diff.
- **Changeset**: `minor` on `@objectstack/service-automation`, correctly argued — it adds a public export **and** changes shipped operator log text (`package "crm"` → `package 'crm'` in the precedence warning). ⛔ Not empty, not `patch`. `Check Changeset` — success.

### ⭐ The pin is built so a green means something

Two deliberately non-redundant layers: call sites assert **through** the renderer, and the renderer's own output is pinned as **literals**. Ablation B is what proves they are not redundant — a fourth caller re-inventing the phrase reddens only the derived row while the three literal pins stay green, and in leg A the derived row stayed **green** because both sides moved together. That is precisely why the literal anchors have to exist, and it was demonstrated rather than argued.

⭐ Two rows close the failure mode an agreement pin is structurally blind to: `not.toContain('undefined')` asserted **independently** of the renderer (so a both-sides regression cannot hide), and an explicit *"the comparison is not vacuous"* row proving `toContain` can tell the two spellings apart. ### Honesty markers I am recording because they are the reason to trust the rest

- **A first ablation leg was a silent no-op** — the `perl` substitution matched zero times and exited 0 — caught by the byte-hash check **before any verdict was read**, voided, and re-run with a different mutator. Self-disclosed.

Measured directly instead: exactly 3 pre-existing `TS2341`, matching the ledger. That silent-green shape is one this seat's ledger has been bitten by before.
- **`tsc --listFiles` proves the new test file is in the CLI program** — a green typecheck that never read it would have said nothing.

### Quoting and fallback — both decided on measurement, ⛔ neither voted

Single quotes, measured **against the producing package** (203 single vs 3 double under `service-automation/src`, one of the 3 being this very phrase), not across the three copies as the card warned against. The safety half is answered honestly rather than overclaimed: `packageId` is an unconstrained `z.string()` with no character pattern, so **neither spelling is provably safe** against an adversarial id — but the same sentence already single-quotes the flow name, the more free-form value, so it adds no ambiguity class the line did not already carry.

The dev's harness mandated a `Co-Authored-By: Claude <model>` commit trailer while this dispatch forbids model names in pushed artifacts.
